/****************************************************************************
 * MAX30208 Precision Digital Temperature Sensor Driver
 *
 * I2C interface, ±0.1°C accuracy, 16-bit resolution.
 * Designed for wearable skin temperature measurement.
 *
 * Datasheet: MAX30208 Rev 2 (Analog Devices / Maxim Integrated)
 *
 * Key specs:
 *   - Supply: 1.7V - 3.6V
 *   - I2C address: 0x50 (7-bit, fixed)
 *   - Resolution: 16-bit (0.00390625°C/LSB)
 *   - Range: -20°C to +60°C (operating: -40°C to +85°C)
 *   - Accuracy: ±0.1°C (30°C to 50°C)
 *   - Conversion time: ~70ms (one-shot) or continuous mode
 *
 * Usage:
 *   1. max30208_init() — verify sensor, configure
 *   2. max30208_read_temp() — read temperature
 *   3. max30208_set_mode() — continuous or one-shot
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __FIRMWARE_DRIVERS_MAX30208_MAX30208_H
#define __FIRMWARE_DRIVERS_MAX30208_MAX30208_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <stdint.h>

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* I2C address (7-bit) */

#define MAX30208_I2C_ADDR           0x50

/* Register addresses */

#define MAX30208_REG_STATUS         0x00  /* Status register */
#define MAX30208_REG_INT_ENABLE     0x01  /* Interrupt enable */
#define MAX30208_REG_INT_STATUS     0x02  /* Interrupt status */
#define MAX30208_REG_FIFO_WR_PTR    0x04  /* FIFO write pointer */
#define MAX30208_REG_FIFO_RD_PTR    0x05  /* FIFO read pointer */
#define MAX30208_REG_FIFO_OVF_CNT   0x06  /* FIFO overflow counter */
#define MAX30208_REG_FIFO_DATA      0x07  /* FIFO data register */
#define MAX30208_REG_FIFO_CFG       0x08  /* FIFO configuration */
#define MAX30208_REG_SYS_CTRL       0x0C  /* System control */
#define MAX30208_REG_ALARM_HIGH_MSB 0x10  /* Alarm high threshold MSB */
#define MAX30208_REG_ALARM_HIGH_LSB 0x11  /* Alarm high threshold LSB */
#define MAX30208_REG_ALARM_LOW_MSB  0x12  /* Alarm low threshold MSB */
#define MAX30208_REG_ALARM_LOW_LSB  0x13  /* Alarm low threshold LSB */
#define MAX30208_REG_TEMP_SETUP     0x14  /* Temperature sensor setup */
#define MAX30208_REG_PART_ID        0xFF  /* Part ID (0x30 for MAX30208) */

/* Status register bits (0x00) */

#define MAX30208_STATUS_TEMP_RDY    (1 << 0)  /* Temperature data ready */
#define MAX30208_STATUS_FIFO_RDY    (1 << 1)  /* FIFO data ready */
#define MAX30208_STATUS_TEMP_OVF    (1 << 2)  /* Temperature FIFO overflow */
#define MAX30208_STATUS_ALARM_HI    (1 << 3)  /* High alarm triggered */
#define MAX30208_STATUS_ALARM_LO    (1 << 4)  /* Low alarm triggered */

/* Interrupt enable bits (0x01) */

#define MAX30208_INT_EN_TEMP_RDY    (1 << 0)
#define MAX30208_INT_EN_FIFO_RDY    (1 << 1)
#define MAX30208_INT_EN_TEMP_OVF    (1 << 2)
#define MAX30208_INT_EN_ALARM_HI    (1 << 3)
#define MAX30208_INT_EN_ALARM_LO    (1 << 4)

/* System control bits (0x0C) */

#define MAX30208_SYS_CTRL_RESET     (1 << 1)  /* Software reset */
#define MAX30208_SYS_CTRL_SHUTDOWN  (1 << 0)  /* Shutdown mode */

/* Temperature setup register bits (0x14) */

#define MAX30208_TEMP_SETUP_CONV    (1 << 0)  /* Start conversion (one-shot) */
#define MAX30208_TEMP_SETUP_RATE_0  (1 << 1)  /* Conversion rate bit 0 */
#define MAX30208_TEMP_SETUP_RATE_1  (1 << 2)  /* Conversion rate bit 1 */
#define MAX30208_TEMP_SETUP_RATE_2  (1 << 3)  /* Conversion rate bit 2 */

/* Conversion rates */

#define MAX30208_RATE_CONTINUOUS    0x00  /* Continuous mode */
#define MAX30208_RATE_ONE_SHOT      0x01  /* One-shot mode */

/* FIFO configuration bits (0x08) */

#define MAX30208_FIFO_CFG_A_FULL    0x0F  /* FIFO almost full threshold (15) */
#define MAX30208_FIFO_CFG_ROLL      (1 << 4)  /* Roll-over on full */

/* Part ID expected value */

#define MAX30208_PART_ID_VALUE      0x30

/* Temperature conversion constants */

#define MAX30208_RESOLUTION         0.00390625f  /* 1 LSB = 2^-8 °C */

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Types
 ****************************************************************************/

/* Operating modes */

enum max30208_mode
{
  MAX30208_MODE_SHUTDOWN = 0,   /* Low power shutdown */
  MAX30208_MODE_ONE_SHOT,       /* Single conversion then shutdown */
  MAX30208_MODE_CONTINUOUS      /* Continuous conversion */
};

/* Conversion rate (for continuous mode) */

enum max30208_rate
{
  MAX30208_RATE_0 = 0,  /* 0: continuous, rate determined by setup */
};

/* Driver configuration */

struct max30208_config
{
  int      i2c_bus;     /* I2C bus number (e.g., 1 for /dev/i2c1) */
  uint8_t  addr;        /* I2C address (default 0x50) */
  int      irq_pin;     /* GPIO pin for data-ready interrupt (-1 = polling) */
};

/* Driver context */

struct max30208_dev
{
  struct max30208_config config;
  int      fd;          /* I2C file descriptor */
  float    last_temp;   /* Last read temperature in °C */
  uint8_t  part_id;     /* Part ID read from sensor */
  int      initialized; /* 1 if init succeeded */
};

/* Temperature reading */

struct max30208_reading
{
  float    temperature;   /* Temperature in °C */
  uint16_t raw_adc;       /* Raw 16-bit ADC value */
  int      valid;         /* 1 if reading is valid */
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_init
 *
 * Description:
 *   Initialize the MAX30208 temperature sensor.
 *   Verifies part ID, configures operating mode.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   config - Driver configuration
 *   dev    - Driver context to initialize
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   0 on success, negative errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_init(const struct max30208_config *config,
                  struct max30208_dev *dev);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_read_temp
 *
 * Description:
 *   Read the current temperature from the sensor.
 *   In one-shot mode, triggers a conversion and waits for completion.
 *   In continuous mode, reads the latest value from the FIFO.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   dev     - Driver context
 *   reading - Output temperature reading
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   0 on success, negative errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_read_temp(struct max30208_dev *dev,
                       struct max30208_reading *reading);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_set_mode
 *
 * Description:
 *   Set the operating mode (shutdown, one-shot, or continuous).
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   dev  - Driver context
 *   mode - Desired operating mode
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   0 on success, negative errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_set_mode(struct max30208_dev *dev, enum max30208_mode mode);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_read_fifo
 *
 * Description:
 *   Read all available samples from the FIFO.
 *   Useful in continuous mode to batch-read accumulated samples.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   dev    - Driver context
 *   buf    - Output buffer for temperature readings
 *   max    - Maximum number of readings to read
 *   count  - Output: actual number of readings read
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   0 on success, negative errno on failure
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_read_fifo(struct max30208_dev *dev,
                       struct max30208_reading *buf, int max,
                       int *count);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_reset
 *
 * Description:
 *   Perform a software reset of the sensor.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_reset(struct max30208_dev *dev);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_get_part_id
 *
 * Description:
 *   Read the part ID register.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_get_part_id(struct max30208_dev *dev, uint8_t *part_id);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_enable_interrupts
 *
 * Description:
 *   Enable/disable specific interrupt sources.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   dev    - Driver context
 *   mask   - Interrupt mask (MAX30208_INT_EN_*)
 *   enable - 1 to enable, 0 to disable
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_enable_interrupts(struct max30208_dev *dev,
                               uint8_t mask, int enable);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_set_alarm
 *
 * Description:
 *   Set high and low temperature alarm thresholds.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   dev    - Driver context
 *   high_c - High threshold in °C
 *   low_c  - Low threshold in °C
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int max30208_set_alarm(struct max30208_dev *dev,
                       float high_c, float low_c);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_close
 *
 * Description:
 *   Close the I2C connection and put sensor in shutdown mode.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void max30208_close(struct max30208_dev *dev);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: max30208_raw_to_celsius
 *
 * Description:
 *   Convert raw 16-bit ADC value to temperature in °C.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

float max30208_raw_to_celsius(uint16_t raw);

#endif /* __FIRMWARE_DRIVERS_MAX30208_MAX30208_H */

5. sensor_manager.h — Sensor manager API (orchestrates all sensors)
6. sensor_manager.c — Sensor manager that coordinates PPG/IMU/EDA/temp sampling
7. CMakeLists.txt — Build script

## Unified Timestamp System (sensor_sync)

Provides a common time base for all sensors to ensure data synchronization:
- Use hardware timer for microsecond precision
- Convert sensor-specific timestamps to common time base
- Support timestamp correction for sensor read delays
- API: sensor_sync_init(), sensor_sync_get_us(), sensor_sync_get_ms()

## Lock-free Ring Buffer (ring_buffer)

Single-producer, single-consumer lock-free ring buffer:
- Fixed-size power-of-2 capacity
- Push/pop operations with overflow detection
- Support for bulk read/write (for FIFO-based sensors)
- Configurable element size
- Overflow count tracking
- API: ring_buf_init(), ring_buf_push(), ring_buf_pop(), ring_buf_push_bulk(), ring_buf_pop_bulk(), ring_buf_count(), ring_buf_overflow()

Define a standard sensor data element:
```c
struct sensor_data {
    uint64_t timestamp_us;  // Microsecond timestamp
    uint8_t  sensor_id;     // Sensor identifier
    uint8_t  data_type;     // Data type (accel, gyro, ppg, etc.)
    uint16_t data_len;      // Data length in bytes
    union {
        struct { float x, y, z; } accel;
        struct { float x, y, z; } gyro;
        struct { float value; } ppg;
        struct { float value; } temp;
        struct { float value; } eda;
        uint8_t raw[32];
    } data;
};
```

## Sensor Manager (sensor_manager)

Coordinates all sensor sampling in a unified framework:
- Manages sensor lifecycle (init, start, stop, close)
- Coordinates sampling rates across sensors
- Provides unified data access interface
- Handles sensor health monitoring (SQI, timeouts)
- Manages power states (normal, low-power, shutdown)

Sensors managed:
- PPG (MAX86141): 100Hz, SPI, interrupt-driven
- IMU (ICM42688): 100Hz, SPI, interrupt-driven
- EDA (AD5940): 32Hz, SPI, interrupt-driven
- Temperature (MAX30208): 1Hz, I2C, polling
- Haptic (DRV2605L): on-demand, I2C
- Fuel gauge (MAX17048): 0.017Hz (1/min), I2C, polling

API:
- sensor_manager_init(): Initialize all sensors
- sensor_manager_start(): Start all sensor tasks
- sensor_manager_stop(): Stop all sensors
- sensor_manager_get_latest(): Get latest reading from any sensor
- sensor_manager_health_check(): Check all sensors are responding

## Model Architecture

Late feature fusion model for emotion arousal classification:
- Input: 15 features from PPG/IMU/EDA/temperature
- Architecture: 2-layer LSTM (32 units) → Dense(16) → Dense(5) → softmax
- Output: 5 classes (excitement, nervous, surprise, stress, other)
- Quantization: INT8 (weights and activations)
- Target: <100ms inference on Cortex-M33 @ 100MHz

Input features (15 dimensions):
```
[0]  HR (bpm)
[1]  HR slope (bpm/min)
[2]  RMSSD (ms)
[3]  SDNN (ms)
[4]  IBI dispersion (ms)
[5]  Activity intensity (0-3)
[6]  Posture (0=sit, 1=stand, 2=walk, 3=run)
[7]  SCL baseline (µS)
[8]  SCR count (per minute)
[9]  SCR amplitude (µS)
[10] Skin temp slope (°C/min)
[11] PPG SQI (0-1)
[12] HR deviation from personal baseline (σ)
[13] RMSSD deviation from personal baseline (σ)
[14] Time-of-day normalized (0-1)
```

## Inference Engine Design

The engine should:
1. Load model weights from C arrays (compiled in)
2. Perform INT8 matrix multiply with 32-bit accumulation
3. Implement LSTM cell with INT8 quantization
4. Implement dense (fully connected) layer
5. Softmax output for probability distribution
6. Support model versioning and integrity check (CRC32)
7. Measure and report inference time

Key operations to implement:
- `int8_matmul()`: INT8 matrix multiply with int32 accumulation and requantization
- `int8_lstm_cell()`: Single LSTM timestep (forget/input/output gates)
- `int8_dense()`: Fully connected layer with ReLU activation
- `softmax_float()`: Softmax on dequantized outputs

## Rule Gate

Before running ML inference, apply rules to exclude unreliable states:
- High activity (running/cycling) → skip, no event
- SQI < 0.70 → skip, prompt "adjust strap"
- Not worn (no skin contact) → skip
- Rapid temperature change (>2°C/min) → skip (environmental)
- Low battery (<5%) → reduce sampling, skip inference

The rule gate outputs a decision: PROCEED / SKIP_WITH_REASON.

## GATT Service Design

Service UUID: custom 128-bit for VelaSense

Characteristics:
1. **Event Notify** (UUID+01) — Notify
   - Real-time event push when arousal detected
   - Format: {timestamp(4), label(1), confidence(1), reason_flags(2), hr(2), rmssd(2)}
   - 12 bytes per notification

2. **Event Summary** (UUID+02) — Read
   - List of confirmed events (paginated)
   - Format: array of event records
   - Max 20 events per read (pagination via offset)

3. **User Label** (UUID+03) — Write
   - Phone sends label confirmation for pending event
   - Format: {event_seq(4), label(1)}

4. **Config** (UUID+04) — Read/Write
   - Device configuration sync
   - Fields: {confidence_threshold(1), event_cooldown(2), sqi_threshold(1), sampling_enabled(1)}

5. **OTA Data** (UUID+05) — Write
   - Firmware update data channel
   - Format: {offset(4), data_len(2), data(N)}
   - With CRC32 verification

6. **Device Status** (UUID+06) — Read/Notify
   - Battery, uptime, event count, SQI status
   - Format: {battery(1), uptime(4), event_count(2), sqi(1), state(1)}

## Sync Protocol

Delta synchronization for efficiency:
- Phone sends last_sync_seq
- Device sends events with seq > last_sync_seq
- Each event has a sequence number for ordering
- Disconnect during sync → resume from last confirmed seq
- Queue up to 100 events during disconnect

## Connection Management

- Auto-advertise on boot (device name: "VelaSense-377")
- Pairing with passkey or Just Works
- Connection interval: 7.5ms - 15ms (low latency)
- Slave latency: 0 (always responsive for events)
- Supervision timeout: 4s
- Reconnect on disconnect (exponential backoff: 1s → 30s)
- Power: reduce TX power when RSSI > -40dBm

Write the peak detection and motion artifact suppression modules for VelaSense.

Output directory: <WSL_HOME>/VelaScene/contest2026_377_moyumanbo/firmware/libs/dsp/

Create these files:
1. peak_detect.h — Peak detection API
2. peak_detect.c — Adaptive threshold peak detection for PPG
3. motion_artifact.h — Motion artifact suppression API
4. motion_artifact.c — IMU-reference adaptive noise cancellation
5. CMakeLists.txt — Build script (update if exists)

## Peak Detection

Detect systolic peaks in filtered PPG signal to compute beat-to-beat intervals:

Algorithm:
1. Compute first derivative of PPG signal
2. Find local maxima where derivative crosses zero (descending)
3. Apply adaptive threshold: threshold = 0.4 × (running_mean_peak - running_mean_trough)
4. Minimum distance between peaks: 300ms (max 200bpm)
5. Maximum distance: 2000ms (min 30bpm)
6. Reject abnormal beats: IBI > 1.5× or < 0.5× of median IBI
7. Output: array of peak timestamps and IBI values

Features:
- Adaptive threshold that adjusts to signal amplitude changes
- Motion-aware: skip peaks during high-motion periods
- Quality flag per peak (based on local SNR)
- Support for missing beat interpolation

## Motion Artifact Suppression

Use IMU data as reference to clean PPG signal:

Algorithm: Adaptive Noise Cancellation (ANC)
1. Model: PPG_clean = PPG_raw - w × IMU_reference
2. LMS (Least Mean Squares) adaptive filter:
   - Filter order: 16 taps
   - Step size (µ): 0.01 (adaptive: increase when motion, decrease when static)
   - Update: w(n+1) = w(n) + 2µ × e(n) × x(n)
3. Use accelerometer magnitude as reference signal
4. Apply only when motion detected (accel variance > threshold)
5. Pass-through when stationary (no filtering needed)

Alternative: Accelerometer-based Wiener filter
- Estimate PPG noise spectrum from IMU spectrum
- Apply frequency-domain Wiener filter
- Better for periodic motion (walking, running)

Features:
- Auto-adapt to different motion types
- Preserve cardiac signal morphology
- Low latency (< 10ms for real-time)
- Graceful degradation: pass-through if IMU unavailable

Store confirmed events in encrypted form on Flash (LittleFS):

    uint16_t reason_flags;   // Reason codes

    uint16_t rmssd;          // RMSSD × 10

- Only event summaries stored (timestamp + label + confidence + features)

- Events are encrypted at rest

## Power Manager

Power states for wrist-worn operation:
```
ACTIVE → IDLE → LOW_POWER → CRITICAL → SHUTDOWN
```

### ACTIVE mode (full operation)
- All sensors at full rate (PPG 100Hz, IMU 100Hz, EDA 32Hz)
- LCD on, BLE advertising/connected
- Inference running every 5s
- Current: ~50mA estimated

### IDLE mode (no active events)
- Sensors at full rate (for continuous monitoring)
- LCD off (or minimal AOD)
- BLE advertising (not connected)
- Inference running every 5s
- Current: ~30mA estimated

### LOW_POWER mode (battery < 20%)
- PPG: 50Hz, IMU: 50Hz, EDA: off
- LCD off, BLE advertising interval increased
- Inference every 30s
- Disable haptic feedback
- Current: ~15mA estimated

### CRITICAL mode (battery < 5%)
- PPG only at 25Hz
- All other sensors off
- LCD off, BLE off
- Inference every 60s
- Only critical alerts
- Current: ~5mA estimated

### SHUTDOWN mode (battery < 2%)
- Save all state to Flash
- Put all peripherals in shutdown
- Enter deep sleep
- Wake only on charger insertion

Battery monitoring:
- Read MAX17048 every 60s
- Smooth with exponential average (avoid false low-battery from voltage dips)
- Trigger mode transitions on SOC thresholds
- Log battery events

## Watchdog

Hardware watchdog management:
- Timeout: 10 seconds
- Feed every 5 seconds from main task
- Track which task should be running
- If task hangs, log fault and reset

Task health monitoring:
- Each task reports alive every 10s via shared counter
- Watchdog checks all counters
- If any task misses 3 consecutive checks → log fault → reset

## Fault Handler

Graceful degradation on errors:
- Sensor failure: continue with remaining sensors
- SPI/I2C bus error: retry 3 times, then disable sensor
- Flash write error: switch to RAM-only mode
- BLE error: restart BLE stack
- Model inference timeout: fall back to rule-based detection
- Stack overflow detection: log and reset

Fault logging:
- Store last 10 faults in Flash (survives reset)
- Format: {timestamp, fault_code, task_id, context}
- Accessible via NSH shell command: `velasense faults`
